title: Step by Step Learning
author: moreicescream
selftext:
Id like to learn vibe coding alot better.

My first game has been really fun but my second one has a lot higher demands and is almost impossible to do with my current prompts.

  
So id like to know where or how I can learn vibe coding? All YouTubers I found seem to.. be decent 

  
For example: Should I first focus on connecting assets and skills? Or should I start with one huge prompt and let it go?

  
I heard let build Claude Code the foundation and then switch to codex for optimization is good etc.

  
Where can I get this knowledge from?

comments.author: SilentDanni
comments.body:
Frankly just learn a little bit about coding. I don't know what your demands are, but I've also been watching youtube and a lot of those youtubers are just showing you "demo porn" or selling some course or never revealing the proverbial secret juice. I don't think you need to know a lot about coding, you just need to know some of the basic concepts and learn to connect some dots on your own. If you can do that then you know how to prompt, what skills are relevant, when to push back on claude shenanigans and so on. 

Furthermore, "vibecoding" is constantly changing and no one knows where this shit is gonna go. Coding will always be here and the concepts your learn will definitely help you learn how to extract more value out of AI. Just my two cents.

comments.author: Hot_Professional8287
comments.body:
>Where can I get this knowledge from

Life. Experience. If prompt-by-prompt is exhausting at scale, similar to baking one cookie at a time in an oven, then what should you do?

Think larger. Lay your game out like a cookie tray. Carefully plan the arrangement of your cookies on the tray, and then the arrangement of each chip within each cookie. Write skills that accelerate the arrangement of cookies and the desired pattern of chips. Then bake the tray with the agentic fire of 1 gabillion GPUs.

comments.author: -Star-Walker-
comments.body: Actually… you can’t learn vibe-coding. You have to understand basics of coding and of course software architecture. I’m sorry.
